name: separator
title: Separator
summary: A thin line that divides content, with an optional label.
description: A 1px rule in the line colour that divides content, horizontal or vertical. An optional label sits in the middle with a rule on each side, like the "or" between two ways of signing in. It takes no room of its own: the caller spaces it. The model is the shared option separator and the rules between menu groups.

anatomy.description: role="separator" with aria-orientation, or role="none" when decorative. Without a label the element is the rule (1px, color.line): full width when horizontal, stretched to its row when vertical. With a label it is a flex row (a column when vertical) whose ::before and ::after are the two rules.

The text in the middle (the children): text.xs, ink-2, centred. It wraps, never truncates, and takes at most 70% of the line (of the height when vertical), so the two rules share the rest. Author text keeps its own direction.

orientation.description: horizontal: 1px high, as wide as its container. vertical: 1px wide, as tall as the row it sits in (align-self: stretch); outside a flex row give it a height.

decorative.description: Purely visual: role="none", so assistive technology skips it (a label is then read as plain text). Otherwise role="separator" with aria-orientation, named by its label when it has one.

notes: role="separator" with aria-orientation (horizontal or vertical); role="none" when decorative.
A separator's children are presentational, so a labelled one is named by its label (aria-labelledby) and the label is announced once, as the separator's name.
Not focusable: this is the static separator, not a splitter.
